title: Evaluation after width truncation
statement: Let $C$ be a finite-depth circuit with first-layer gate type $g$, let $w$ be a width threshold, and let $x\in\{−1,1\}^n$. If every first-layer gate omitted by truncating to gates of width at most $w$ evaluates at $x$ to the neutral value of the dual gate $g^*$ (that is, $-1$ for OR and $1$ for AND), then the truncated circuit and $C$ have the same value at $x$.
hypotheses_covered: An input x in the n-dimensional sign cube
